key_insight: In a pilot study of 25 simulated therapy videos, AI ratings approached clinician agreement on therapeutic behavior attributes but showed lower agreement on domain-level competency.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline may supplement competency assessment in therapist training, rather than replace clinician supervision.
method: A vision-language model annotated verbal and nonverbal behaviors and incorporated them into transcripts.
A large language model rated competency using the ENACT scale.
Two clinicians verified detected behaviors; four independently rated each video.
evidence_signal: Clinicians jointly confirmed 70% of 1,558 AI-detected behaviors; AI–clinician attribute agreement was AC1=0.73 versus 0.75 between clinicians, while median domain-level ICCs were 0.57 versus 0.67.
watch_item: The small, simulated-session sample limits generalizability; validation in real-world training settings is needed.
paper_title: Using Vision and Large Language Models for Psychological Intervention Competency Assessment: A Pilot Study of Agreement with Clinician Ratings
